t: The problem: reaching home lab remotely
title: The problem: reaching home lab remotely
description: ISPs hide home networks behind NAT/CGNAT with no public IP; ZeroTier/Tailscale punch through with encrypted tunnels so your phone reaches your GPU box anywhere. Remote access without port forwarding. The problem is NAT.

demo.program: print('NAT/CGNAT -> no public IP -> tunnels solve it')
demo.expected_output: NAT/CGNAT -> no public IP -> tunnels solve it

title: ZeroTier: virtual L2 networks
description: ZeroTier creates virtual Ethernet networks; devices get ZeroTier IPs and behave as if on one LAN. A 16-digit network ID joins devices. L2 semantics enable broadcast protocols.

demo.program: print('join network ID -> virtual LAN membership')

title: Tailscale: WireGuard mesh
description: Tailscale builds a WireGuard mesh (tailnet); every device gets a stable 100.x.x.x address and a MagicDNS name. WireGuard gives the crypto; Tailscale gives the coordination. Mesh means direct device-to-device paths.

title: MagicDNS and taildrop
description: MagicDNS resolves device names (gpu-box) to tailnet IPs; Taildrop sends files device-to-device. Names beat IPs; built-in file sharing helps. The extras compound.

title: Subnet routers and exit nodes
description: Subnet routers expose LANs behind a tailnet device; exit nodes route internet traffic through a chosen node. The tailnet extends beyond its members. Gateways bridge worlds.

title: DERP relays for hard NATs
description: When direct P2P fails, Tailscale's DERP relays carry encrypted traffic (still end-to-end encrypted). Relays are the fallback, not the path. Connectivity degrades gracefully.

title: Serving local AI remotely
description: The canonical use: phone on cellular opens http://gpu-box:8000 for the vLLM server via tailnet — local AI, anywhere. No exposure to the internet. The pattern recurs across this whole series.

title: ZeroTier vs Tailscale choice
description: ZeroTier for L2 semantics and self-hostable controllers; Tailscale for WireGuard speed and polished UX/SSO. Both solve remote access. Choose by network model needs.

title: Security model
